transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

My daughter and my friend basically forced me to come here because they're all worried, but I don't think they understand. I know people think it sounds strange, but I’m certain there are forces directing my art and that this exhibit has a special destiny, no matter what anyone says.

Over the past week or two, have you needed much less sleep than usual and felt unusually energetic or driven? Have you also been talking faster, having racing thoughts, or spending more money or taking bigger risks than usual?

Oh, absolutely, I wake up buzzing with so much energy that I barely sleep or sit down because I'm driven to get this legacy exhibit perfect. My daughter says I talk a mile a minute, but there's just this rush of ideas pushing the words out, and I can't slow down. And yes, I've been swiping my card for expensive canvases and posters because, even though money is tight with my wife's medical needs, this show is going to change everything anyway.

Before this current high-energy period, have you ever had a separate episode of depression or another similar “up” episode at a different time in your life? Or is this the first time anything like this has happened?
I don't recall ever having an episode like this before in my life. This is really the first time I've felt this kind of intense drive and energy, so I'm just focused on getting my exhibit ready.

Before this started, have you ever had a period lasting at least several days when you felt unusually down or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day? Or any earlier separate time when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep like you do now?

I don't recall ever having periods of feeling really down or losing interest in things in the past. And I've definitely never had a separate energized period like this before this current one started a few months ago. This is the first time I've ever experienced anything like this.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a first lifetime episode lasting months with persistently elevated/expansive energy, markedly decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, racing thoughts/flight of ideas, increased goal-directed activity focused on an art exhibit, and excessive spending despite financial strain. He also expresses grandiose/delusional beliefs that external forces are directing his art and that the exhibit has a special destiny. No prior depressive, manic, or hypomanic episodes were reported, supporting a current manic episode with psychotic symptoms rather than bipolar disorder with recurrent episodes.
